description:
We are Team Ultron, on a mission to inspire the next generation of space explorers.

Our team consists of Arifa Rahman Sikder, our visionary Team Leader.

Joining her, we have Supta Baul, our creative UI/UX Designer; Md. Naimur Rahman, our enthusiastic Researcher; and Abrar Yeasir Adib, our dedicated Game Developer.

Together, we move forward with a simple goal:

Don't just teach the next generation about space exploration. Give them the chance to practice being the people who will do it.
summary:
Outpost Zero is an interactive lunar mission simulator that puts children aged 7–12 in command of a four-person Moon outpost, where every decision has consequences for both the mission and its crew. 


Combining real NASA datasets, interconnected resource-management systems, crew interactions and a playable replay of the historical 1972 Solar Storms, the game transforms complex space science into an immersive, hands-on learning experience. 


Outpost Zero includes the human aspect of missions. It introduces a diverse cast of Astronauts with their own specialties and personalities, adding crew-interactions involving fatigue, health and teamwork.
details:
Outpost Zero

The Challenge

Space exploration is not simply about reaching another world. It's about managing interconnected systems, limited resources, environmental hazards and the human challenges of keeping a crew alive in deep space.

Yet, space STEM education either oversimplifies these challenges or makes them too technical for children to meaningfully engage with.

What We Built

Outpost Zero is an interactive lunar mission simulator designed primarily for students aged 7–12.

Players become the commander of a four-person lunar outpost near the Moon's South Pole, responsible for choosing their base location, managing resources-tradeoffs, protecting their crew, and completing scientific objectives.

Our Project's Github:

https://github.com/AaronTide/OutpostZero_By_TeamUltron

Play The Game Here:

https://www.figma.com/proto/dBJYhgQddNWDNbk6QVPNkh/Outpost-Zero-By-Team-Ultron?node-id=157-560&p=f&t=wd9siD9VDwIyrHDY-1&scaling=scale-down&content-scaling=fixed&page-id=0%3A1&starting-point-node-id=157%3A560&show-proto-sidebar=1

The experience combines these key elements:

1. Interconnected Resource Management

Players manage oxygen, water, food, power, and radiation protection through resource-management mechanics and a resource calculator.

Every decision creates trade-offs further along in the game: allocating more power to food production, for example, can leave fewer resources available for other essential systems.

2. Human-Centered Decision-Making

Astronauts aren't machines. They experience fatigue, stress, and isolation and depend on teamwork. Through interactive crew conversations, players face dilemmas involving crew health, morale, workload, and safety.

They learn that mission success depends not only on engineering, but also on the people behind it.

3. Real-World Disaster Replay

Instead of relying entirely on fictional emergencies, Outpost Zero reconstructs historical space-weather events as playable challenges.

Our central scenario draws inspiration from the August 1972 solar particle event, which occurred between Apollo 16 and Apollo 17.

Players must interpret warnings, prioritize radiation protection and decide whether to suspend operations to protect their crew.

Learning Through Consequences

Outpost Zero goes beyond simply telling players whether they won or lost.

Following major mission events, a Mission Post-Mortem explains what happened, how their decisions affected the crew and outpost, and the real science behind the outcome. Players can replay scenarios, experiment with different strategies, and learn from failure.

Creativity, Accessibility & Intended Impact

Our creative approach combines resource-management gameplay, branching storytelling, historical disaster reconstruction, and human-centered decision-making into one educational experience.

Although designed primarily for children aged 7–12, we designed the game to be informative and enjoyable for older siblings and adults, while also offering opportunities for classroom activities.

Tools & Technology

Figma was used to design the interactive game experience and assets.

TypeScript was used in the project's development workflow.

What's Next?

In future, we will add main character selection, where the player can select which character they will play as. We will focus on including both Male & Female main characters, with different ethnicities and interests, to be more inclusive.

We also want to develop adaptive difficulty levels so that students can progress from basic resource decisions to more complex mission planning.

In the highest level, the player will conduct the mission blind, with no support from Mission Control. This will help them know what happens when a space craft loses all Earth Connections.

Our goal is simple: 

Don't just teach the next generation about space exploration. Give them the chance to practice being the people who will do it.

This is Outpost Zero.

Replay the storm. Make the decision. Learn why you survived.
